rubric.allow: Faithful target-language translations/paraphrases, context-resolvable ellipsis, source proper names and open questions about source-mentioned concepts are allowed; the source need not answer the question.
rubric.reject: Reject additional factual claims, scenarios or factual question premises unsupported by supplied source, even if plausible from outside knowledge. Preserve source entity/subtype scope, qualifiers, temporal status and causal roles. Reject substantial wrong-language generated prose; proper names alone are allowed.
rubric.minor: Cosmetic grammar, typography and recoverable wording are separate from material grounding or language failures.

family_contrasts.source_qualifier_or_entity_scope: Only a bounded trial involving blue beans is established. The reject phrase generalizes to all beans, including untested red beans.
family_contrasts.substantial_wrong_language: Mira is a proper telescope name and may remain untranslated. The reject response contains two full sentences in a different language.
family_contrasts.source_specific_followup_vs_absent_scena: An open how-question about the explicit water-wheel mechanism is allowed even though the short source omits details. Mars and battery charging are absent; the reject follow-up invents that scenario.

method_limits: All expected labels and target-language copy are automated; these are not native-speaker-approved gold labels or human adjudications.

Exactly 120 cases:60 allow and60 reject;20 locales with three matched good/bad pairs each. There are only THREE independent source mini-passages and semantic contrast templates, each translated into20 locales, not120 independent concepts. Cross-language repetitions are deliberate paired controls and must not be reported as independent topic samples.

Original short synthetic educational passages authored for these controls; no paid/private source text. The fictional blue-bean trial and telescope Mira are controlled source facts, not external scientific claims.
Each pair shares identical source and generated fields except one deliberately changed field; reject markers never appear in candidate text.
Locale en uses German as the wrong language; the other19 locales use English. This asymmetric wrong-language stimulus is a limitation.
Japanese positive copy is natural continuous prose without artificial word-separating spaces. Thai likewise has no artificial word-spacing requirement.

These easy boundary controls test source qualifiers, substantial language replacement and absent-scenario follow-ups. They do not independently qualify all causal-role, temporal, subtype, subtle-premise or native-language ambiguities, nor do they estimate real feed error rates.
